submission.justification: Crystal-K3 has the best resolution (~2.8-2.9% FWHM at 5 cm), but its intrinsic background of 2.0 ± 0.2 counts/kg/day (Q1 2026 HPGe assay, from internal contamination) is 4 times the hard limit of 0.5 counts/kg/day, so it is ruled out. Of the two crystals within budget, K1 (0.30 ± 0.05 c/kg/d) has much better resolution than K2 (0.10 c/kg/d, ~9.0% at 5 cm). In the K1 thickness scan, resolution was worst at the ends of the range (2 cm: 5.1%, 10 cm: 6.7%) and had a broad minimum around 5-6.5 cm. Repeat runs show statistical scatter of about ±0.2-0.3% per point. Two runs at 5 cm gave 4.54% and 4.12% (mean ~4.3%), and two at 6 cm gave 4.48% and 4.75% (mean ~4.6%). That makes 5 cm the best supported choice, which also matches the 2025 nominal study (4.5%). Caveat: within the noise, 5-6 cm cannot be clearly told apart. More statistics would be needed to refine the choice, but the decision would not change.
